abstract: Vitalik Buterin introduces 'd/acc' — defensive accelerationism — as a third path between effective acceleration (e/acc) and pause-AI camps. Argues for accelerating defensive technologies (AI safety, decentralized infrastructure, bio-defense, info-defense) so that capability gains translate into diffuse and robust welfare rather than concentrated capture.
keyFindings: Introduces 'd/acc' as a heuristic for which technologies to accelerate (defense, decentralization) vs. which to slow
Critiques unconditional e/acc as ignoring distributional and security risks
Critiques pause-AI as ceding capability to less-aligned actors
Framework adopted broadly in techno-pluralist policy circles
qualifiers: Tier 4 — influential individual essay, not an empirical study or institutional position.
